page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance belonging to the c4 family. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The instance provides 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB. This instance runs on the Xen hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the c4.4xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1440.69 and a multi-core score of 15219.95, supported by hardware-level AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. Memory performance shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 851.49 GB/sec, which drops to 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In LLM inference testing, the instance handles a small 135M model at 872.74 tokens/sec for prompt processing, but performance drops to a weak rating of 23.37 tokens/sec when processing prompts for a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.4xlarge offers a dense allocation of dedicated compute resources relative to its memory capacity, making it suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. Typical workloads for this profile include software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations, as evidenced by a Geekbench compiling score of 13105.0 and a static web serving throughput of 11.52 GB/sec.
